minors.title: The prediction phase's heartbeat re-bases total, so a healthy prediction pass still reads "suspected stall" and run.py ls progress goes backwards
minors.detail:
trainer.py:364-372 beats the prediction phase with total = len(predict.splits) + 1 and one beat per split, keeping unit "step". Two consequences I measured against the export.

(a) The stall rule now bites on the prediction pass, which contracts 9(d) calls the longest phase of a generator run. jobs/registry.stall_line_s over a train loop that beat every LOG_EVERY = 50 steps at an 18-minute gap gives a line of 5400 s; with one beat per split, a split whose prediction takes 2 h gives registry.judge -> ('suspected stall', False). The predict-only incarnation is worse: its own file holds only the opening beat plus one per split, so typical_gap_s has fewer than DEFAULTS["min_intervals"] = 3 gaps and the line falls back to warmup_s = 1800 s -- a first split of 40 min gives ('suspected stall', False), and two splits of 1 h and 100 min give ('suspected stall', True), i.e. escalated. That is the same harm TRAINER-4 named ("a healthy predict-only continuation ... shown as suspected stall, inviting a needless kill"); the fix removes the no-beat-at-all case but not the long-silence case. On the trained path the verdict is new, because the pre-fix code's last beat carried done == total and judge returned "done" first. Script: /tmp/rerev/stall_check.py (pure registry functions, nothing written).

(b) jobs/registry._ls_row folds a train run's progress from the newest beat, so `run.py ls` shows a train piece jump from 3000/3000 step to 0/3 step and then 1/3 step when its prediction starts, with "step" now counting splits. Observed directly in the reruns: the heartbeat of the A3.4-shaped run holds ..., {"done": 20, "total": 20, "unit": "step"}, {"done": 0, "total": 2, "unit": "step"}, ...

The implementer records both as decision 5 and offers the owner a one-word alternative, so this is a call for the main session, not a silent defect. A finer cadence (a beat per prediction chunk rather than per split) would close (a).

minors.title: The alignment gate now writes PASS when every event of its slice is dropped, so a max_len too small for the data is no longer caught anywhere before done.json
minors.detail:
With reference_loss applying batches()'s drop rules (the PACKING-03 fix), a gate slice in which every event's longest text exceeds max_len gives packed = 0 (an empty sum) and plain = 0 (reference_loss's new `return torch.zeros(())`), so trainer.py:411-415 computes diff = 0 and writes {"PASS": true, "packed": 0.0, "plain": 0.0, "diff": 0.0, "n_rows": 3}. Measured through the shipped gate (/tmp/rerev/adv_cases.py, cases 4 and 5): at max_len = 22 against an event whose longest text is 23 tokens, all three methods report packed=0.00000000 plain=0.00000000 diff=0.000e+00 n_rows=3 -> pass; at max_len = 23 the same fixture compares 3 real rows and passes with real numbers. The pre-fix tree failed loudly here (the PACKING-03 record's packed=0 against plain=0.886), which was the wrong message but was a stop.

Failure scenario: the shipped defaults make the slice events_per_mb * accum = 4 * 2 = 8 rows, and example_id sorts the cuts of one event together, so the slice is one event. Lower train.max_len to fit a card, and that event goes over: the gate passes vacuously, the run trains on whatever survives, and the only record of how much was dropped is done.json's counts.dropped_overlong, written when the run is already over. n_rows in align_check.json is the slice height, not the compared row count, so the file reads as if 8 rows matched.

minors.title: cgen/cparam reference_loss no longer left-truncates the prompt, against a sentence ticket 13 pins, with no errata entry covering it
minors.detail:
Ticket 13 section 3 pins cgen's reference_loss as "train_causal_callgen.py:203-237 (collate) ... one row per sequence, left-truncated prompt, right padding", and section 4 gives cparam the same shape. The fix deletes the budget and the `prompt_full[-budget:]` slice (cgen.py:263-264, cparam.py:289-290) so the prompt is never cut. That is what makes the gate consistent with batches(), which drops an over-long event whole instead of truncating -- my rerun of the reviewer's band case (longest text 97 tokens, text+sep 101, target 7, max_len 99) goes from cgen 6.919e-03 / cparam 1.525e-02 (SystemExit) to 0.000e+00 on both -- and the implementer documents it as decision 1 and flags it for the owner.

I am recording it because it is a shipped deviation from a pinned ticket sentence and .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md has no entry for it, so nothing in the tree records the ruling. Blast radius is small: reference_loss has exactly one caller, trainer._run_alignment_gate, so no training, validation, prediction or metric number moves. It needs the owner to write the errata line, not a code change.

decisions: PACKING-03 root rule: reference_loss scores exactly the rows batches() keeps and shows them the same tokens -- it now applies the same whole-event overlong drop, the same MAX_TGT_TOK drop and no prompt truncation. The packed side cannot move (errata line 118 pins the drop-whole rule, and left-truncating would destroy the shared token prefix the packing is built on) and the gate's slice cannot move (trainer.run would have to know which rows a method drops, which 2.6 forbids and no hook reports). Consequence for the owner: ticket 13's pinned 'left-truncated prompt' for cgen/cparam's reference_loss, ported from legacy's collate, is no longer followed -- contracts 2.6/2.5 win.

PACKING-03: the drop rules are written out a second time inside each reference_loss rather than shared with _build_events, because sharing would make the two sides agree by construction and the gate would stop testing anything (2.6: 'the one piece of code written twice on purpose').

TRAINER-2: _run_alignment_gate's finally no longer calls set_training(True); run() owns the training mode and sets it immediately after the gate, before the step loop. Ticket 13 step 8 says the gate's eval mode is 'restored afterwards' -- it now is, one level up, because the paths that skip the gate need the same call and two owners of one flag is what hid the defect. The align_check: true path's observable order is unchanged.

TRAINER-2: probe.grad_checkpointing(True) moved out of the load block into the training branch, after set_training(True), so a predict-only continuation no longer arms a feature only a backward pass uses.

TRAINER-4: the prediction beats use unit 'step' (8.4 assigns the unit per stage, not per phase, and 'step' is train's word) and total = len(splits) + 1 (the splits plus the frame their rows are joined into and written to), so the last beat before finish() reads done < total. A monitor now shows a train piece switching from N/steps to 0/3 when prediction starts; a distinct word such as 'split' would be a one-word change if the owner prefers it.

TRAINER-3: LOG_EVERY stays 50 (the ticket's pinned constant) and the first step, every 50th step and the last step log instead. The post-loop line is guarded on window_loss_n > 0 so a resume that trains no new step writes no step line with a loss of 0.

tests/test_packed_loss.py keeps exactly three test methods and adds the three new fixtures as subtests, so A3.6's pinned expectation ('three tests') still reads true while the PACKING-03 regression coverage lands.
README.md untouched: no import, venv, reads or writes line of the four code files changed.

open.title: run.py ls now reloads the setting and re-parses every listed module once per ledger row: 0.05 s -> 2.97 s for 40 rows
open.detail:
_compute_row_flags caches the loaded setting in `settings[(workflow, setting, debug)]` and then throws the cache away on the next line: `current = None if cfg is None else _current_key(workflow_name, setting_name, stage, debug)`, and _current_key calls _current_setting again, so every row pays a fresh schema.load. _behind_versions then calls schema.versions_of(row['stage'], cfg) per row, and schema._parse_module is not memoised, so each call re-reads and re-ast.parses every module the stage lists. The base cached the finished key by (workflow, setting, stage, debug) and did the work once.

Measured on fresh exports of both commits with schema.load and schema._parse_module counted, 40 ledger rows of one (workflow, setting, stage), private outputs root: df3c473 -> schema.load calls=1, module parses=16, wall clock 0.05 s. 63ed7f9 -> schema.load calls=41, module parses=965, wall clock 2.97 s. That is ~74 ms per row, so a ledger of 300 runs costs about 22 s per `run.py ls` — the command the gpu-run skill hands the user to poll (ticket 16 row 5). On top of that, _inputs_changed sha1s every file named in each run's consumed.json and meta.json split_files on every ls; a build run's consumed.json names the record files, and the implementer's report flags that cost but not the load/parse one.

The fix is inside the new function: use the already-cached cfg (schema.key(stage, cfg)) instead of calling _current_key, and memoise versions_of by (stage, workflow, setting, debug) the way the base memoised the key.
open.failure_scenario: After the first real batch of runs, `run.py ls` over a 300-row jobs/runs.jsonl spends about 22 s in schema.load and ast.parse before printing a line, where the same ledger cost well under a second at df3c473. Measured: 40 rows of one setting take 2.97 s at 63ed7f9 against 0.05 s at df3c473, with schema.load called 41 times instead of 1 and modules parsed 965 times instead of 16.

open.title: The section-4 --debug walk SEAMS-5 is about still refuses one stage earlier: eval.theta_from is a name form kept on the real root
open.detail:
Not introduced by this fix — df3c473 behaves identically — but the rewrite made _upstream_dirs the single place that answers where an upstream run lives, and it deliberately keeps a name-form reference on the non-debug root (its docstring says so). train_probe.yaml gives cgen_qwen3_0pt6b and cparam_qwen3_0pt6b `eval: {theta_from: train_probe/ctool_qwen3_0pt6b}`, the name form, so schema.upstream('eval', cgen) resolves theta_from.eval to the REAL ctool eval key and _upstream_dirs points at <root>/outputs/eval/<real key>. The construction plan's section-4 acceptance (notes/plans/2026-09-17-construction-plan.md:602-609) runs `run.py train_probe cgen_qwen3_0pt6b --debug` with no override for eval.theta_from, and a pure --debug acceptance produces no real run, so that directory never exists. Errata '3.4 / 9(c)#8' pins only inject.probe_score, inject.probe_gen and score.baseline; eval.theta_from is not in its list, so the owner has to decide either to add a fourth pinned override to the acceptance command or to let a name-form reference follow the walk's root.

Verified on fresh exports with the debug build/train/eval runs of both probes on disk. 63ed7f9: `resolved theta_from.eval: <root>/outputs/eval/a4a903bff5de exists=False` then "run.py: eval: upstream 'theta_from.eval' at <root>/outputs/eval/a4a903bff5de has no done.json; run it first", while the debug ctool eval run the acceptance produced sits at <root>/outputs/debug/eval/a8b67d485d63. df3c473 prints the same refusal.

Line 3, `run.py train_probe cgen_qwen3_0pt6b --debug`, spends the GPU time on sample, build and train and then exits at the eval stage with "upstream 'theta_from.eval' at <root>/outputs/eval/a4a903bff5de has no done.json; run it first", so the two pinned inject keys SEAMS-5's fix unblocks are never produced.

minors.detail:
_pinned_run_dir calls `schema.load_frozen(candidate)._key == key_val` on the first candidate whose settings.yaml exists, with no guard. load_frozen raises yaml errors on a settings.yaml that does not parse and schema.SchemaError through _refuse_unknown_frozen_fields on one that carries a field the current dataclasses no longer have — which is exactly the older run a pinned key: reference exists to name. _has_pinned_reference, added in the same commit a few lines up, catches (schema.SchemaError, OSError, yaml.YAMLError) for the same call, so the new code is inconsistent with itself.

minors.title: A resumed LoRA run loads the pre-crash Adam moments onto a freshly initialised adapter, so the first resumed step moves lora_A on momentum computed for a different matrix
minors.detail: The fix makes the LoRA resume work, and the model's function is preserved across the restore (save() merged the adapter, peft re-initialises B at zero, so the restored logits equal the saved probe's -- I measured 0.0 for the generator's forward and 4.5e-07 for the classifier). What does not survive is the adapter's own parametrisation: the restored lora_A is a new random matrix while the optimizer state loaded at trainer.py:223 holds the moments of the old one. Measured on the export with /tmp/probefix_check/adapter_across_resume.py (tiny two-layer 64-hidden Qwen3, three real steps, then trainer.run's restore): 'pre-crash lora_A norm 2.348026 | lora_B norm 0.040673 | its exp_avg norm 0.0162905' then 'restored lora_A norm 2.29263 | lora_B norm 0.0 | equals the pre-crash lora_A: False', 'the moments now attached to the restored lora_A: exp_avg norm 0.0162905 | step 3.0', and a single resumed step taken with all-zero gradients moves lora_A by 0.0107411 (about 0.5% of its norm). The perturbation is bounded and the run goes on training (loss 0.40883 -> 0.32824 in the implementer's round trip, 0.41669 -> 0.31318 in mine), so this is not a correctness break -- it is the price of ticket 06's merged-save layout, which the implementer already flagged under 'Open, for the reviewer'. Recording it because the behaviour is new (before this commit the same path raised ValueError instead), it is invisible in any CPU acceptance item, and the alternative the finding named (carry the adapter plus the optimizer state in last/) would change the checkpoint layout contract 1.6 pins, which is the owner's call.

minors.title: A checkpoint whose meta.json tuning is neither full nor lora is now refused with a message naming probe.tuning, the setting field, not the checkpoint it came from
